doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Eighteen-year-old J. J. Johnson and his parents' consent
summary: Johnson's parents vetted Carter before letting him go to California, like Carter's own mother had.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How about . . . you mentioned J. J. Johnson, who was very young, I think. What, eight[een]?
You met his parents and did . . .
Oh, I had to meet his parents, because they had to okay him leaving home, you know, to go with me all the way to California from Indianapolis.
What assurances did they ask of you?

They didn’t ask. I think they just wanted to see me and meet me and not really interview me, but sort of interview me and see what kind of guy I was that was offering to take her son, or their son, miles away, you know. I guess I passed scrutiny, you know.
Similar to your own circumstance, I guess, when your . . .
That’s when I was going to Pittsburgh.
Yes, that’s true. Quite, quite the same, yes.
